title: Mate in one
line: Every check, and which one ends it.

steps.text: To find a mate in one, first list every check you can give. Here your queen has four.
Now test each one. Which check leaves the king no square, no block and no capture? Play it.

wrong.f6f7: The rook or the king takes the queen.

steps.hint: Look for the check where nothing can take the queen and the king has no square.
steps.after: Checkmate. The queen checks from the corner, and the king's own rook and pawn block it in.

steps.text: Another one. List the checks your queen can give, then play the one that mates.

wrong.g3e5: Black takes the queen, with the queen or a pawn.
wrong.g3g8: The rook or the king takes the queen.

steps.hint: Your pawn near the black king guards one square next to it.
steps.after: Checkmate. The pawn guards the queen, so the king cannot take her.

steps.text: Sometimes there is only one check. Find it.
steps.hint: Only one of your pieces can reach the black king.
steps.after: Checkmate. The king's own pieces wall it in, and the knight jumps over them.

steps.text: Now you are Black. List the checks and play the one that mates.

wrong.d6c5: White blocks the check with a pawn or a piece, or the king steps aside.

steps.hint: Your knight guards one of the squares next to the white king.
steps.after: Checkmate. The knight guards the queen, and the king has no square to go to.

summary: List every check before you move. Mate is the check with no square, no block and no capture left.
